title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Chronic Crisis Stream Programme implemented by Christian Aid with local partners BBS and PSSAG in Rakhine State, Myanmar, aims to meet the complex interconnected needs of crisis- and conflict-affected communities, reduce the risk of violent conflict, foster resilience and reduce vulnerability to the impacts of climate change, through integrated, people-centred approaches which put communities and civil society organisations in the driving seat. The objectives of the grant are to support communties to: (1) respond to humanitarian need, (2a) tackle violence and build peace; (2b) tackle gender-based violence; (3) strengthen resilience; and (4) adapt to climate change. In 2024, 18,233 individuals were successfully reached.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: MMR. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: Climate change adaptation was the principal objective of programme interventions: Communities and local leaders have improved knowledge of climate change effects, the causes and impacts of climate change and the role of adaptation; target households were supported to adopt sustainable climate-resilient farming methods, promote diversified agricultural production to reduce climate risk, and cultivate and distribute climate-resilient seeds; and communities have been supported to implement erosion/flood protection measures in areas that are becoming increasingly susceptible to erosion/ flooding with due regard to the potential environmental impacts of these measures.
